- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward quickly — overcorrects or lags in mean reversion.
- Model exhibits persistent upward bias in the middle of the forecast (days 10–20), often failing to account for recent downward momentum.
- Forecast tends to be too smooth — underreacts to short-term volatility or sudden policy/news shocks.
- Model often underestimates the magnitude of downward corrections after spikes, especially in the last 5–10 days.
- In low-volatility periods, model may overfit recent trends and fail to recognize mean reversion.
- Forecast horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts show consistent bias toward higher prices, especially when recent history is trending up.
- Model reacts too slowly to policy changes or supply-demand shocks — lagging by 2–5 days in adjusting to new fundamentals.
